domain.name: HR & People Operations
domain.description: Practical hiring, onboarding, role design, performance systems, scheduling, documentation, offboarding, and people operations with legal and privacy boundaries.

competencies.name: Role Design & Job Expectations
competencies.description: Define responsibilities, outcomes, decision rights, skills, and success measures for a role.
competencies.purpose: Make hiring and management expectations clear.

units.title: Role design workflow
units.content: Define mission, recurring responsibilities, measurable outcomes, required capabilities, decision rights, collaboration points, and what is explicitly out of scope.

units.title: Outcomes beat task dumps
units.content: A useful role definition explains what success looks like, not just a long list of activities.

units.title: Role-design failures
units.content: Avoid impossible catch-all roles, vague ownership, hidden physical or schedule requirements, and success measures unrelated to actual work.

drills.title: Build a role scorecard
drills.prompt: Design a concise scorecard for a new operations role.

competencies.name: Recruiting & Structured Screening
competencies.description: Source candidates and evaluate job-relevant evidence consistently.
competencies.purpose: Reduce bias and improve hiring signal.

units.title: Structure improves fairness
units.content: Using the same job-relevant criteria and core questions makes comparisons more defensible and less dependent on first impressions.

units.title: Screening workflow
units.content: Define criteria; use consistent questions; collect work evidence where appropriate; score against the role; document rationale; protect candidate information.

units.title: Screening failures
units.content: Avoid protected-class questions, irrelevant personal probing, inconsistent scoring, and treating intuition as the only evidence.

drills.title: Score a candidate consistently
drills.prompt: Evaluate a hypothetical candidate against a predefined role scorecard.

competencies.name: Employee & Contractor Onboarding
competencies.description: Prepare access, equipment, training, expectations, safety, and first-week checkpoints.
competencies.purpose: Get new contributors productive without uncontrolled access.

units.title: Onboarding workflow
units.content: Confirm role and start details; prepare minimum necessary access; provide policies and safety information; assign owner; sequence training; verify understanding; schedule check-ins.

units.title: Access should follow need
units.content: Do not give broad system permissions just because onboarding is easier that way.

units.title: Onboarding failures
units.content: Avoid sharing passwords, missing access revocation owners, overwhelming the first day with unprioritized material, and leaving success expectations unstated.

drills.title: Build a first-week onboarding plan
drills.prompt: Create a first-week plan for a new team member.

competencies.name: Scheduling, Timekeeping & Coverage
competencies.description: Plan staffing coverage, shifts, time records, breaks, and handoffs while respecting applicable rules.
competencies.purpose: Maintain reliable coverage and accurate records.

units.title: Coverage planning
units.content: Define demand windows; identify required skills; build schedule with availability and constraints; plan backup coverage; record changes; reconcile time records.

units.title: Coverage is a system constraint
units.content: A schedule is not complete if it covers headcount but misses required skills or critical handoffs.

units.title: Scheduling failures
units.content: Avoid off-the-clock expectations, undocumented changes, ignoring fatigue, and presenting generalized labor rules as current local law without verification.

drills.title: Repair a coverage gap
drills.prompt: Resolve a hypothetical shift gap without violating stated constraints.

competencies.name: Performance Feedback & Development
competencies.description: Set expectations, document coaching, recognize performance, and build improvement plans.
competencies.purpose: Create a consistent evidence-based performance system.

units.title: Feedback workflow
units.content: Describe observed behavior and impact; restate expectation; listen for context; agree next action; set follow-up; document proportionately.

units.title: Specific and timely beats dramatic
units.content: Frequent concrete feedback is more useful than vague praise or surprise criticism months later.

units.title: Feedback failures
units.content: Avoid personality labels, retaliation, undocumented shifting standards, and promises about employment outcomes outside authority.

drills.title: Write a coaching record
drills.prompt: Document a performance conversation using behavior, impact, expectation, and follow-up.

competencies.name: Policies, Handbooks & Documentation
competencies.description: Maintain readable people policies and records while distinguishing policy from law.
competencies.purpose: Reduce ambiguity and preserve consistent operations.

units.title: Policy is not automatically law
units.content: Internal rules should be consistent with current applicable law, but a handbook should not be treated as authoritative legal advice.

units.title: Policy maintenance
units.content: Define purpose, scope, owner, effective date, procedure, exception path, review cadence, and source references for legally sensitive requirements.

units.title: Policy failures
units.content: Avoid copying stale templates, conflicting policies, collecting unnecessary sensitive information, and changing expectations without communicating effective dates.

drills.title: Review a policy draft
drills.prompt: Identify operational and legal-review gaps in a hypothetical attendance policy.

competencies.name: Workplace Conflict & Issue Intake
competencies.description: Receive concerns, document facts, route issues, and preserve confidentiality boundaries.
competencies.purpose: Handle workplace issues consistently without informal escalation chaos.

units.title: Issue intake workflow
units.content: Listen without promising outcomes; capture who, what, and when; separate facts from interpretation; assess immediate safety; preserve confidentiality on a need-to-know basis; route to authorized review.

units.title: Document facts, not verdicts
units.content: An intake note should preserve what was reported without declaring guilt before review.

units.title: Issue-intake failures
units.content: Avoid retaliation, public discussion, investigating beyond authority, and promising secrecy that cannot be guaranteed.

drills.title: Take a workplace concern
drills.prompt: Create an intake record and routing plan for a hypothetical complaint.

competencies.name: Offboarding & Access Revocation
competencies.description: Coordinate final work, property return, knowledge transfer, access removal, and records.
competencies.purpose: Close relationships cleanly and reduce security or operational gaps.

units.title: Offboarding workflow
units.content: Confirm effective time; inventory access and assets; transfer ownership and records; revoke access at the correct time; collect company property; document completion; preserve required records.

units.title: Access revocation is time-sensitive
units.content: Offboarding should coordinate system access with the actual end of authorized work, not rely on someone remembering later.

units.title: Offboarding failures
units.content: Avoid shared credentials, delayed revocation, deleting records that must be retained, and leaving company data in personal accounts.

drills.title: Create an offboarding checklist
drills.prompt: Build a checklist for a departing contractor with system access.
